# Sprint 3 Execution Log: Two Clients, One Full Game

**Project:** CS 457 Term Project: Networked Pente
**Author:** Bode Kaanta
**Generated by:** `python tools/demo_game.py -i localhost -p 5457` on 2026-11-16

This log was recorded with the real `server.py` and two real `client.py` processes on one machine. `tools/demo_game.py` starts them and types each player's move when that client prints `>>> YOUR TURN`. Lines starting with `> ` are the typed input (piped input is not echoed, so the script adds them). The clients reach the server through DNS name resolution (`-i localhost`) and TCP, the same way they do when a person types. The raw console files are in [`execution_log/`](execution_log/).

## What this log shows

| Sprint 3 acceptance item | Where to look |
|---|---|
| Client parses `-h`, `-i`, `-p`; server parses `-h`, `-p` and binds `0.0.0.0` | Section 1 (help output) and the first server log line (`listening on 0.0.0.0:5457`) |
| Client resolves the server by DNS hostname, no hard-coded IP | `[INFO] Resolved localhost -> ...` at the top of each client console |
| Client catches `socket.gaierror` and fails gracefully | Section 1: `server.kaanta.edu` does not resolve on this machine yet (DNS for that name is set up on router R1 in the Sprint 4 CML lab). The client prints the error and exits with status 1, with no traceback |
| Server accepts 2 simultaneous clients and runs FSM transitions cleanly | Section 2: `conn-1` and `conn-2` each get a handler thread. Every transition is logged with its row ID from `fsm_specification.md` (L1, L3, G1, G2, G5-G8, G11, G12) |
| At least 3 turns of gameplay | 11 moves were played: P1 opened on the center and her second stone was rejected inside the tournament-rule box (she kept the turn), a capture at move 5, an occupied point and an off-board move rejected (P2 kept the turn), then P1 won with five in a row on a diagonal |
| CLI board, turn status, and score summaries | Section 3: the board with column letters A-S and row numbers 1-19, `>>> YOUR TURN` / `Waiting for Bob (P2) to move...`, live captures on every turn, then round points and the session leaderboard |

## 1. Command-line help and DNS failure

```text
$ python3 server.py -h
usage: server.py [-h] -p PORT [-v]

Networked Pente game server. Listens on 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces) and hosts one
two-player game room.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -p PORT, --port PORT  TCP port to listen on (the project uses 5457)
  -v, --verbose         also log every message sent (DEBUG level)

Example: python3 server.py -p 5457
(exit status 0)

$ python3 client.py -h
usage: client.py [-h] -i HOSTNAME -p PORT [-a ALIAS] [-s {dots,xo}]
                 [-b {lines,ascii}]

Terminal client for networked Pente. Connects to the game server, shows the
board, and sends your moves.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -i HOSTNAME, --host HOSTNAME
                        server DNS hostname, e.g. server.kaanta.edu (resolved
                        with DNS)
  -p PORT, --port PORT  server TCP port (the project uses 5457)
  -a ALIAS, --alias ALIAS
                        your player name: 1-16 letters, digits or '_' (asked
                        if omitted)
  -s {dots,xo}, --stones {dots,xo}
                        stone symbols: xo = X and O (default), dots = filled
                        and hollow circles
  -b {lines,ascii}, --board {lines,ascii}
                        board drawing: lines = grid lines like a real board
                        (default), ascii = plain ASCII for consoles that show
                        boxes or '?' instead of lines

Example: python3 client.py -i server.kaanta.edu -p 5457 -a Alice
(exit status 0)

$ python3 client.py -i server.kaanta.edu -p 5457 -a Alice
[ERROR] Unable to resolve DNS hostname 'server.kaanta.edu'.
Please check your Cisco router DNS configuration ('ip dns server' / 'ip host') or verify domain spelling.
        Resolver detail: [Errno 11001] getaddrinfo failed
(exit status 1)
```

## 3. Client consoles

### Alice (P1, `X`): connecting, waiting, and the first three turns

Alice's first stone must go on the center point (the prompt reminds her). Her second stone, `H12`, is only 2 points from the center, inside the box, so the server rejects it with `TOURNAMENT_RULE` and she keeps the turn. `G13`, a corner of the box, is accepted.

## How to reproduce by hand

```bash
python3 server.py -p 5457
python3 client.py -i localhost -p 5457 -a Alice
python3 client.py -i localhost -p 5457 -a Bob
```
